clues.title: Architecture: Architecture
text: Traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct. Most houses feature tin roofs and wooden painted frames, giving them a unique look.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Red license plate
text: License plates in Bhutan are almost always red and are easily visible on vehicles.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Stone blocks guardrail
text: Bhutan commonly uses stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads. These blocks are very common and are one of the best ways to recognize rural roads in Bhutan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Southern Flatlands
text: Flat landscapes like this in Bhutan can only be found in the south.
NOTE: The coverage in the south is limited to the four regions shown on the map.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Vibes
text: Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.
NOTE: In the south are flat areas where you cannot see any mountains.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Stone Blocks

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.
Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Car
text: Coverage in Bhutan was taken by a grey Google car without an antenna.
Bhutan is the only left hand driving country which has a grey Google car.
Make sure to not mix it up with a white Google car, since they can look similar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
